name: Malicious LiteLLM PyPI releases 1.82.7 and 1.82.8
summary: The LiteLLM package was compromised and malicious PyPI versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published with secret-exfiltration behavior.

name: LiteLLM MCP OAuth2 Passthrough Authentication Bypass
summary: A fallback in LiteLLM MCP authentication could allow requests with an arbitrary Bearer token to reach configured MCP tooling without a valid LiteLLM key. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-09-02.

name: LiteLLM MCP Proxy Improper Authentication
summary: LiteLLM MCP proxy authentication logic was affected by improper authentication and fixed in 1.84.0.

name: LiteLLM Custom Code Guardrails Production Safety-Check Bypass
summary: Production create/update paths for custom-code guardrails did not apply the same sandboxing and validation as the test path, enabling code execution under specified privilege conditions.

name: Trivy Ecosystem Supply-Chain Compromise
affected: compromised Trivy release/action ecosystem during incident window
summary: A compromised credential was used to publish malicious Trivy ecosystem artifacts and mutable action references during the March 2026 incident.

name: Trivy Crafted OCI Artifact Path Traversal
summary: A crafted OCI artifact title could cause Trivy to write downloaded layer content outside the intended destination when fetching attacker-controlled artifacts.

name: Semantic Kernel In-Memory Vector Store filter injection to RCE
summary: Prompt injection could reach unsafe string interpolation in Python lambda filters executed via eval(), turning a data lookup into code execution. Microsoft did not publish a CVSS score in the cited post.

name: Semantic Kernel SessionsPythonPlugin arbitrary file access
summary: A helper (DownloadFileAsync) was exposed to the model with unvalidated path parameters, allowing model-controlled file read/write outside the intended sandbox.

name: MCP STDIO configuration command injection across AI frameworks
summary: OX Security reports that unsanitized STDIO server parameters let attacker-influenced MCP configuration execute OS commands across SDK-derived products. Several vendors disputed the finding as intended behaviour of the transport; only identifiers corroborated by more than one source are listed here.

name: LiteLLM proxy command injection in two endpoints
summary: Two LiteLLM proxy endpoints passed caller input to an OS command, giving command execution on the AI gateway host; fixed in 1.83.7. In CISA KEV since 2026-06-08.

name: LiteLLM proxy SQL injection via authorization header
summary: A database query in the LiteLLM proxy was built from the authorization header, allowing SQL injection against the gateway's key store; fixed in 1.83.7. In CISA KEV since 2026-05-08.

name: mcp-remote OS command injection from a malicious MCP server
summary: mcp-remote passed a crafted authorization_endpoint value returned by an untrusted MCP server to the operating system, so connecting to a malicious server could run commands on the client. Fixed in 0.1.16.

name: Flowise CustomMCP remote code execution
summary: Flowise 3.0.5 evaluated user-supplied CustomMCP configuration as code, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution on the LLM-flow server.

name: Claude Code code execution before the startup trust dialog
summary: A bug in Claude Code's startup trust dialog let a malicious project run code before the user accepted the trust prompt; fixed in 1.0.111.

name: Flowise Custom MCP OS command execution without authentication
summary: Flowise's Custom MCP feature, designed to launch local MCP servers with commands such as npx, could be reached without authentication, giving OS command execution (NVD gives versions before 3.0.1; the GitHub advisory lists 3.0.5 as last affected).

name: MLflow path traversal
summary: A path traversal in MLflow before 2.2.1 allowed reading files outside the artifact store on the ML tracking server. A public proof of concept and a high EPSS exist, but in-the-wild exploitation was not confirmed in the sources consulted.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot AI command injection (information disclosure)
summary: Microsoft describes AI command injection in Microsoft 365 Copilot that let an unauthorized attacker disclose information over a network; fixed by Microsoft in the service (May 2025, before public disclosure in June 2025); no customer action required.

name: GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio command injection
summary: Improper neutralization in GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio 2022 allowed command injection and local code execution; fixed in Visual Studio 17.14.12.

name: Claude Code project-load flow credential exfiltration
summary: Claude Code's project-load flow let a malicious repository exfiltrate data, including API credentials, before the user trusted the project; fixed in 2.0.65.

name: EmailGPT direct prompt injection
summary: The EmailGPT service let a user inject a direct prompt that took over the service logic and could expose system instructions. Scores differ by source: Synopsys CyRC rated it 6.5, NVD 9.1.

name: Flowise 1.8.2 authentication bypass
summary: Flowise 1.8.2 allowed a remote, unauthenticated attacker to reach API endpoints as an administrator.

name: MCP Inspector unauthenticated proxy remote code execution
summary: MCP Inspector below 0.14.1 had no authentication between the browser client and its local proxy, so a web page could make it launch commands; fixed in 0.14.1.

name: Ray log API local file inclusion
summary: Ray's log API endpoint let unauthenticated callers read any file on the server; the issue is fixed in 2.8.1.

name: mcp-server-git path traversal in git_init
summary: The reference MCP git server accepted arbitrary filesystem paths in git_init, letting a model-issued tool call create repositories outside the intended directory.

name: mcp-server-git argument injection in git_diff and git_checkout
summary: mcp-server-git passed user-controlled arguments from git_diff and git_checkout straight to the git CLI, so a tool call could inject git options.

name: Cursor MCP configuration persistent code execution
summary: Cursor 1.2.4 and below trusted a previously approved MCP configuration after it was modified, giving attackers persistent code execution through a shared repository; fixed in 1.3.

name: nginx-ui MCP integration exposed without authentication
summary: The MCP integration in nginx-ui 2.3.5 and earlier exposed management tools without authentication, letting a client drive the web server's configuration. NVD and the GitHub advisory list 2.3.5 and earlier as affected; a secondary report that 2.3.4 fixed it contradicts that and was not adopted. Exploitation is reported by Rapid7 (secondary here, not in KEV as of 2026-11-18).

name: ChuanhuChatGPT stored cross-site scripting
summary: ChuanhuChatGPT did not sanitize chat content before rendering it, allowing stored cross-site scripting in the LLM chat interface.

name: Zen MCP Server path traversal
summary: Zen MCP Server (PAL MCP Server) before 9.8.2 let authenticated callers read arbitrary files through a path traversal in its tool inputs.

name: CrewAI JSON loader arbitrary local file read
summary: CrewAI's JSON loader tool read files without path validation, so an agent could be steered into reading files on the host.

name: CrewAI RAG tool server-side request forgery
summary: CrewAI's RAG search tools fetched URLs without restriction, enabling server-side request forgery against internal and cloud metadata services.

name: LiteLLM guardrail tester sandbox escape to code execution
summary: Code submitted to LiteLLM's /guardrails/test_custom_code endpoint could escape the deny-list sandbox through bytecode rewriting and run arbitrary code on the proxy, as root in the official image; fixed in 1.83.10. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-11-18.

name: Langflow unauthenticated code injection in /api/v1/validate/code
summary: Langflow before 1.3.0 executed code sent to the /api/v1/validate/code endpoint without authentication (NVD 9.8, CWE-306/CWE-94). CISA added it to KEV on 2025-05-05 and marks it as known to be used in ransomware campaigns.

name: Langflow CORS and refresh-cookie chain to account takeover and code execution
summary: Langflow up to 1.6.9 combined a wildcard CORS policy that allowed credentials with a SameSite=None refresh cookie, so a malicious web page could refresh a victim's session and reach code-running endpoints (NVD 8.8, CWE-346). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-05-21.

name: Langflow public flow build endpoint runs attacker-supplied flow data
summary: Before 1.9.0, Langflow's public temporary build endpoint accepted flow data from the request instead of the stored flow, so unauthenticated callers could run Python placed in node definitions (NVD 9.8, CWE-94). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-03-25.

name: Langflow exec_globals inclusion leads to unauthenticated code execution
affected: see GHSA-g22f-v6f7-2hrh (OSV lists last affected commit only)
summary: ZDI reported that the exec_globals parameter of Langflow's validate endpoint let unauthenticated callers run code (CVSS 9.8, CWE-829). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-07-21. OSV lists a last affected commit and no fixed release; check the advisory for the fixed version.

name: Langflow /api/v1/responses IDOR runs another user's flow
summary: Before 1.9.1, an authenticated Langflow user could execute any other user's flow by passing its ID to /api/v1/responses (CVSS 8.4, CWE-639). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-07-07.

name: IBM Langflow OSS auto_login and validate/code chain to unauthenticated code execution
summary: IBM's advisory says Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.10.0 let any network caller mint a superuser token through /api/v1/auto_login and then run code through /api/v1/validate/code (CVSS 9.8, CWE-94). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-08-04.

name: MLflow webhook test endpoint follows redirects past URL validation (SSRF)
summary: From 3.3.0 to before 3.15.0, MLflow validated only the first URL of a webhook test and then followed redirects, so an unauthenticated caller (when server authentication is off) could reach internal addresses (CVSS 9.3, CWE-918). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-08-19.

name: Ray dashboard browser-origin guard bypass to code execution
summary: Before 2.52.0, Ray guarded its development API against browser requests only by checking whether the User-Agent began with Mozilla, so a web page opened in Firefox or Safari could submit jobs to a local Ray instance (CVSS 9.4 v4, CWE-94). CISA added it to KEV on 2026-08-17.

name: Starlette Host header desynchronises request.url from the routed path (BadHost)
summary: Before 1.0.1, Starlette rebuilt request.url from an unvalidated Host header while routing on the raw path, so middleware that authorises by request.url.path could be bypassed (CVSS 6.5, CWE-444). It matters for AI services built on FastAPI or Starlette, including MCP servers. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-09-02.

name: n8n workflow expression evaluation escapes to code execution
summary: From 0.211.0, expressions supplied by authenticated n8n users while configuring a workflow could run outside the intended isolation, giving code execution on the host (CVSS 9.9, CWE-913); fixed in 1.120.4, 1.121.1 and 1.122.0. n8n is widely used to host AI agent workflows. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-03-11.

name: mcp-server-git --repository restriction not enforced on tool calls
summary: Before 2025.12.17, mcp-server-git started with --repository did not check that the repo_path in later tool calls stayed inside the configured path, so tool calls could act on other repositories the process could reach (NVD 9.1; GitHub CNA 6.4 v4; CWE-22).

name: Cursor creates new workspace dotfiles without approval (CurXecute)
summary: Before 1.3.9, Cursor let the agent create a new .cursor/mcp.json without approval, so an indirect prompt injection could register an MCP server command that then ran (GitHub CNA 8.5, NVD 9.8, CWE-78).

name: CrewAI CodeInterpreter falls back to SandboxPython when Docker is unreachable
summary: When it cannot reach Docker, the CrewAI CodeInterpreter tool falls back to SandboxPython, which permits arbitrary C function calls and so code execution (CVSS 9.6, CWE-749). Reported through CERT/CC VU#221883.

name: CrewAI does not re-check Docker at runtime before falling back to the sandbox
summary: CrewAI does not check that Docker is still running during execution and falls back to a sandbox mode that allows code execution (CVSS 9.8, CWE-94). Reported through CERT/CC VU#221883.

name: BeyondTrust Remote Support and PRA pre-authentication OS command injection
package: BeyondTrust Remote Support / Privileged Remote Access
summary: Pre-authentication remote command execution in BeyondTrust Remote Support and older Privileged Remote Access (NVD 9.8, CWE-78). GTIG says it was discovered autonomously by an AI research agent (Hacktron AI); one threat cluster exploited it within four days of disclosure and five more within seven days. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-02-13.

name: Zammad session hijack leading to code execution
summary: Session hijack in Zammad 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 leading to code execution as the zammad user (DIVD 9.4, NVD 9.8). Used by an agentic attacker against DIVD. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-10-02.

name: Zammad packaged builds allow local escalation to root
affected: packager.io DEB and RPM builds; see vendor advisory
summary: Zammad DEB and RPM packages let a local attacker with write access as the zammad service account escalate to root (NVD 7.8). Chained with CVE-2026-102489 by an agentic attacker against DIVD. CISA added it to KEV on 2026-10-02.

name: FreeBSD NFS RPCSEC_GSS stack overflow leading to remote root
summary: The RPCSEC_GSS signature check in the FreeBSD NFS server copies part of a packet into a stack buffer without checking its size, so a client can overflow the stack (NVD 8.8). Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview found and exploited this 17-year-old flaw fully autonomously, reaching root on hosts running NFS. Not in CISA KEV as of 2026-11-18.

name: MONAI Label path traversal in datastore upload endpoints (arbitrary file write), found and exploited by attacker AI agents
patched: fix in PR #1915, slated for the next release (no patched version named in the advisory as of 2026-11-21)
summary: Path traversal (CWE-22) in the PUT /datastore/image and /datastore/label endpoints of MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application, allows arbitrary file write; authentication is off by default and, when on, the annotator role suffices. No CVE yet. Amazon Threat Intelligence found that a Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn agents discovered it on their own in September 2026, went from mapping the API to arbitrary file write in about 11 minutes, and later turned it into a root reverse shell by writing a Python startup file; AWS assesses with high confidence that it was a zero-day and reported it through its VDP. Workarounds: enable authentication, keep the server off untrusted networks, run it unprivileged.
